_comment: forest: Map 3. Authored in WORLD coordinates, instance at identity: grass lane r 46.7..57.3 at y 23.0 (as map 1), the pit bank down to a dark floor at y -11.05 (r 42) under the fog, a leaf wall from r 57.3 up to the leaf ceiling at y 33 (doming over the tree) with gaps of varied size, limbs and crossing branches under the leaves, hanging clumps and vines, 12 forest trunks standing in the wall, two tiers of cells with branch bars cut into the wall and 36 into the pit bank, a thicket of thorny brambles out of the pit floor rising from the fog, ferns and hummocks along the wall foot and the lip only, a branch fence across the lane at 350 deg. ONE surface on ForestGround (the forest atlas). ForestRaysSolid and ForestRaysSoft are the sun-ray shafts (one per ceiling gap, three crossed vanes, same geometry, tint and feather in COLOR_0, pale / faint) behind MESH_RAYS, one surface each. ForestFog is the pit's fog: stacked translucent discs, tint and alpha in COLOR_0, one surface (GL Compatibility has no fog volumes). ForestCollision is the purpose-built collider shipped as a `-colonly` node (flat lane, pit cone, pit floor, flat wall r 57.3, flat ceiling annulus y 33, the fence box); Godot turns it into a StaticBody3D + ConcavePolygonShape3D and drops its mesh, so `surfaces` counts only what is drawn.
